name: B10-0399/2026 (Renew) – Deteriorating situation of media freedom and freedom of expression in Hong Kong following the recent arrest of bookseller Leticia Wong and the convictions of Lee Cheuk-yan and Chow Hang-tung
title: JOINT MOTION FOR A RESOLUTION on the deteriorating situation of media freedom and freedom of expression in Hong Kong following the recent arrest of bookseller Leticia Wong and the convictions of Lee Cheuk-yan and Chow Hang-tung
part_text:
The European Parliament calls for the release of bookseller Leticia Wong, activists Lee Cheuk-yan and Chow Hang-tung, and Albert Ho, all held or convicted under Hong Kong's national security laws. It condemns these cases as part of a wider crackdown on free speech and the media in Hong Kong. It asks Hong Kong to drop the charges, asks the European Union to impose sanctions on Hong Kong and Chinese officials, and asks European countries to suspend extradition treaties with China. The text is a statement of the Parliament's position; it does not itself change any law.

- **What changes:** Nothing yet. The Parliament is asking others to act, not passing a law.
- **Who it affects:** Wong, Lee, Chow, Ho and other prisoners; Hong Kong and Chinese officials who could face European Union sanctions.
- **What happens next:** The resolution goes to European Union governments, the Commission, the Council, China and Hong Kong.
